data.hypothesis: The two measured OpenMP variants use per-worker cutoffs of 512 and 256 options, with similar means and no per-size timings available. Requiring at least 1024 options per effective worker tests the contrasting assumption that a coarser grain avoids parallel overhead on medium workloads while retaining static-scheduled parallelism for large workloads. The controller should compare the resulting serial/parallel boundary against the baseline and earlier variants; no gain is assumed.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use as evidence that the OpenMP outer loop can preserve varied-input correctness, not as proof that a particular cutoff is optimal or that every size benefits.
memory_lessons.claim: The two measured OpenMP variants were correct on eight varied cases and averaged 1.4078 ms and 1.4301 ms, respectively, versus the serial baseline mean of 7.5286 ms. These aggregate results do not isolate small-work overhead or the effect of their different cutoffs.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure a substantially coarser per-effective-worker cutoff and inspect available sizes and thread counts near the resulting serial/parallel boundary.

data.notes: The catalog has two distinct measured source programs, both valid; the 256-options-per-effective-worker candidate is slightly faster in aggregate than the other candidate, but no per-case timings are supplied. This candidate uses a generic per-effective-worker cutoff of 1024, so at the observed four-thread cases n=16, 128, and 1024 remain serial while n=131072 uses static OpenMP scheduling. Each parallel iteration writes its unique result index; the team request is bounded by min(threads,n), and the nested-parallel guard avoids creating a nested team. No commands or measurements were run here; the controller must verify correctness and measure overhead and gains under the frozen protocol.
transformations: Factored the unchanged Black-Scholes per-option formula into a helper shared by serial and parallel paths.
Added an OpenMP outer loop with static scheduling, requesting no more than min(threads,n) workers and avoiding nested teams.
Used a generic cutoff of 1024 options per effective worker to retain a serial path for small workloads and contrast earlier lower cutoffs.
